Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with this game. Sri Lanka suffered their 9th consecutive loss in ODIs at home and need a big turnaround in the next match if they want to stay alive in this series. The third ODI is on Sunday in Pallekele and we look forward to your company at 0945 local (0415 GMT). Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

South Africa skipper, Faf du Plessis says that they are renowned for fighting back. Admits that the Test series was disappointing. Adds that today it was tricky as well but they adapted nicely. Considers the pitch to be a decent one but towards the end, it got a bit tired. Is pleased that they are chasing well at the moment and putting the pressure on the Sri Lankan spinners. Terms their bowling performance as exceptional and praises his bowlers for pulling it back whenever Sri Lanka tried to stage a comeback. Lauds his team for executing the plans superbly. On him getting out in the 40s with great consistency on this tour, du Plessis replies that he is not thinking much about it and is just trying to stay positive.

Sri Lanka skipper, Angelo Mathews says that they gave away too many wickets upfront and never got going. Also adds they didn't hold on to the catches which cost them. Further says that their bowlers were bowling in good areas but the fielding let them down. On Niroshan Dickwella's injury, Angelo informs that he has gone for a scan and hopes that he will be okay. Mentions that there are a lot of positives and they still can stay alive in the series if they win the next game. On his own batting form, Mathews admits that he couldn't really get away with the shots as the wickets kept falling but is pleased with his batting. On his fitness, he replies that he is doing fine.

Man of the Match, Quinton de Kock says that he is not too sure what has changed but good work is finally paying off. Reckons that it's not spinning as much as it was during the Test matches. Adds that the last two months have been difficult and it's always challenging anywhere in the subcontinent. On the pitch, he feels that it stayed the same throughout and maybe spun a little more in the second half but was a good one for batting overall.

The old cliche - Catches win matches! Sri Lanka dropped quite a few and their ground fielding was also mediocre. That didn't allow their bowlers to build any kind of pressure and eventually it cost them dearly. They dropped de Kock when he was on 18 and 24, and the South African wicket-keeper made them pay. The bowling of Akila Dananjaya was the only positive that the hosts can take from this game as apart from him, the rest struggled. Also, the way the South African batsmen have decoded the spin mystery is really commendable.

Chasing a target of 245 could have been a tricky task for the visiting team but their openers provided a steady start and laid a strong platform. Quinton de Kock, in particular, looked in blazing form and dominated Sri Lanka's spinners. He never allowed the pressure to build by finding the fence at regular intervals. As a result, in spite of a few wickets going down, South Africa were never rattled. Faf du Plessis and JP Duminy's knocks threw Sri Lanka's chances out of the window. Towards the end, the two all-rounders, Mulder and Phehlukwayo finished the formalities with utmost ease.

Tables have turned in the shorter format. Another comprehensive win for the Proteas as they go 2-0 up in the 5-match ODI series. First up, their bowlers did a commendable job in restricting Sri Lanka to a below par total. Niroshan Dickwella played a knock of substance but the rest didn't contribute much. Angelo Mathews' innings was on the slower side and that failed to give Sri Lanka the much-needed kick in the death overs. Credit to the Protean bowlers also for bowling superbly with both the new and old balls.

FOUR! That will do. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 4 WICKETS! A good length ball outside off, Mulder gives a little bit of charge and whacks it through cover-point for a boundary. Job done and the batsmen shake hands. This is now South Africa's 10th consecutive ODI win against Sri Lanka. Domination.
Excellent delivery. Extra bounce from a good length outside off, Mulder tries playing through the line but is beaten.
Hurries the batsman with a well-directed short ball, Andile mistimes his pull shot over square leg for a single. 3 more needed.
Stifled appeal from the bowler. He angles across a length ball outside off, Phehlukwayo swings and misses. Nothing from the keeper and the umpire.
Shortish and sliding down the leg side, Mulder eases it off his hips to fine leg for one.
Kasun Rajitha is back on.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. No run to end the over. 2 runs in the last two overs, South Africa are in no hurry.
Another delivery spinning away to beat the bat of Andile Phehlukwayo.
Flatter and on off, Andile plays the reverse sweep but finds short third man.
Play and a miss! Turning away from the batsman around off, Phehlukwayo goes for a big shot but is beaten. The keeper takes the bails off immediately, appeals but nothing doing.
Goes on the back foot and punches it down to long on for a run.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it safely.
Shehan Jayasuriya is back on.
Serves it on a length and outside off, Phehlukwayo forces it straight towards mid on.
Shortish and angling away, Andile cuts it off his back foot to covers.
Once again a length ball on middle has been defended watchfully by Phehlukwayo.
On a length around middle and off, Phehlukwayo defends it off his back foot.
Good length ball on off, Andile strokes it off his back foot to mid off.
Fractionally short in length and outside off, Mulder punches it from the back foot to sweeper cover for a run. South Africa are one big hit away from going 2-0 up in the series.
Loopy ball around middle and leg, spinning down, Andile tries to flick but misses. It goes off his pads to leg gully. 7 more needed.

FOUR! That will release all the pressure. Flighted ball landing around off, slower through the air and off the pitch, Andile immediately opts for the reverse sweep and spanks it through cover-point for a boundary.
Skidding away from the batsman, Andile plays it from the crease towards point. Clearly not picking Jayasuriya.
Hurries down the track to a full ball around leg and drives it straight towards the cover fielder.
Spin and bounce from around leg, Phehlukwayo stays back to defend but misses the ball completely. Gets hit high on the front leg.
Shortish and outside off, Mulder cuts it from the crease to deep point for a run.
Shortish and around off, it's punched off the back foot past the diving point fielder. A couple taken to end the over. A better throw could have been interesting.
Stays on the back foot and punches it to the off side.
Andile has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Andile Phehlukwayo is the new batsman.

OUT! After cruising in most parts of this chase, South Africa are now limping towards the target. 14 more needed. This time Perera bowls it full and around off, Duminy skips down the track and blazes his cover drive through the line. It's travelling and Kusal Mendis takes a very sharp catch inside the ring to give Thisara his 150th ODI scalp.
FOUR! Easily done! Perera once again delivers a short ball around middle, Duminy rides the bounce and pulls it powerfully through backward square leg for a boundary.
Bangs it in short and on middle, it's pulled to deep square leg for a brace.

Appeal for an lbw! Fires it full and on middle, skidding down, Mulder tries to flick but misses. He is hit on the pads, they appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Hang on, the replays show three reds. Poor Sri Lanka, they had no reviews left.
Flatter and slower around off, Mulder stays back and punches it to covers.
Strides on the front foot and drives it back to the bowler.
Mulder dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
Tossed up ball outside off, driven through covers.
Gets down on one knee and slogs it over mid-wicket for a run.
On a length around off, Mulder stands tall inside his crease and punches it back.
Slants in a full ball on off, Willem draws forward and defends it back.
Angling away from the batsman, Duminy plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total.
A mistimed pull shot in the air but it goes safely to deep square leg. Another single taken.
Shortish around leg, pulled behind square leg for one.
A length ball on middle, played in front of square leg for a run.
Fires in a flat and short ball in line of the stumps, Mulder goes deep inside the crease and punches it to sweeper cover for one. 25 more needed.
Leans forward to a full ball around off and drives it with the spin to short cover.
Loopy and full on middle, Mulder lunges and offers the full face of the bat in defense.
Full and around leg, JP sweeps it through backward square leg for a single.
Turning back in from around off, Duminy tries to flick but gets a leading edge. It rolls back to the bowler.
SIX! Blasted out of the ground! A delivery on the fuller side around middle and off, Duminy hurries down the track and belts it over wide long on for a biggie.
Digs in a short ball around off, Duminy pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single. Retains strike.
Straighter in line, Mulder uses his wrists to work it through square leg for a run.
Good length ball landing outside off and shaping back in a bit, Mulder defends it off his back foot.
Slower one from 'round the wicket. It's outside off and JP calmly runs it down past backward point for a single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Angles in a length ball on off, Mulder defends it by getting a bit forward.
Full and around leg, swept behind square leg for a brace. 5 from the over without much risk. That's all they need.
Hangs on the back foot and punches it to long off for a run.
Arm ball on middle, Mulder strides forward to defend but it takes the inside edge and lobs towards short mid-wicket. The fielder there dives forward but it falls in front of him.
Quicker and shorter around off, Mulder plays a late square cut for a couple of runs.
Flatter and on middle, Mulder moves back and punches it back to Jayasuriya.
Tossed up ball around off, defended back off the front foot.

Pitches it full and outside off, Mulder stays back and pushes it with an angled bat through backward point. A single again.  We gave credit to Mathews for having a slip in place for the first ball. But then he wasn't proactive enough to stop easy singles by bringing the field up after the fall of a wicket.
Angles in a shortish ball around off, from 'round the wicket. Duminy taps it down with gentle hands towards cover-point for a run.
Turns it off his pads in front of square leg for a run. A bit of a strange field setting now. They need to stop singles at this stage.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Shortish on off, pulled wide of mid on for a run.
Willem Mulder is the new batsman.

OUT! Sri Lanka are hanging in there. Credit to Mathews for having a slip in place. Lakmal dishes out a back of a length ball outside off, Miller rocks back to punch it through the line but gets a big fat outside edge behind. Kusal Mendis at wide first slip makes no mistake on a day where dropping catches has become a fashion. This is also the 100th ODI wicket for Suranga Lakmal, he becomes the 17th Sri Lankan to reach this milestone.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Strides forward to a full ball and defends it off the outer half of the bat.
Eases it off his pads through backward square leg. They take a single. Thisara charges towards the ball, fumbles and they take an extra run as well.
Appeal for an lbw! Spinning back into the new batsman, Miller tries to defend but misses. They appeal but perhaps it's missing leg.

Drinks break. 50 more left for South Africa to go 2-0 up in the series. The wicket of du Plessis has jolted them a bit but they will believe that they have enough batting to come to get the remaining runs. David Miller is the new batsman.

OUT! Another caught and bowled for Akila Dananjaya. Bowls it flat and short in line of the stumps. It stops a bit from the surface and Faf after going deep inside the crease mistimes his shot back towards the bowler. A clean catch taken this time by Dananjaya. The South African skipper misses out on what would have been his first fifty on this tour by a run. So far, Faf on this tour - 49, 1, 48, 7, 47 and now 49. He made 79 and 71 in the warm up games though.
Tossed up ball around middle and off, defended off the back foot.

Fetches a short ball from outside off and pulls it firmly in front of square leg. Prabath Jayasuriya runs across to his right and dives to stop the ball. Nearly flicks it past the rope as he tries to get up but no harm done. A couple of runs saved.
Very full and on middle, it's clipped through mid-wicket and the fielder in the deep rushes across to his left to stop the ball. Enough time for the batsmen to take three runs.
Full and angling in around off, du Plessis brings down a straight bat and keeps it out towards mid-wicket.
On a length and outside off, it's patted down towards point.
Shortish and on middle, Duminy pulls it behind square leg for a single.
Walks down to the pitch of the ball and then blocks it.
Suranga Lakmal is back on.
On a flatter trajectory, punched off the back foot through point for a single.
Leans ahead to this one and keeps this one out.

In the air... but safe! Short ball, climbing on Duminy. He goes for a pull across the line but mistimes it over the mid-wicket region. Kusal Mendis runs behind while Upul Tharanga is running in from the deep. There is no calling whatsoever as Mendis backs out. The ball falls in no man's land. Another example of Sri Lanka's dismal show on the field. Two runs taken.
Shorter in length, kept out watchfully.
Wide! That was close to the leg stump, close shave. Pitches outside leg as Duminy goes for the sweep but misses. The ball turns in and just goes past the leg stump.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They pick up a single.
Turning into Duminy as he clips it through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! 16 from the over! Another gorgeous shot from the South African skipper. Fractionally overpitched outside off, du Plessis strokes it through extra cover to find the fence again.
FOUR! Shot! Pitched up ball, du Plessis leans ahead and punches it on the up past mid on to pick up another boundary.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Wide outside off, Duminy uses his feet and swings at it but misses.
Almost dragged that back! Good length ball, shaping in. Faf tries to chop it away but gets an inside edge past his stumps towards fine leg. A run taken.
SIX! Faf is in terrific form! Advances down the track to the fullish ball and lifts it nonchalantly over long on to clear the fence.
Stays back to this one and keeps it out watchfully.

Another huge shout falls on deaf ears! Tossed up around off, spinning in. Duminy kneels and tries to sweep it away but the ball goes off something as the fielder at first slip dives to his right and takes it. An appeal ensues but the umpire shakes his head. The replay shows that the ball brushed the shoulder of the batsman.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Shorter in length outside off, Faf cuts it late past backward point to pick up three runs.

A huge appeal for LBW denied! Tossed up nicely outside off, spinning in sharply. Du Plessis leans ahead to counter it but misses to get hit on the pads. Dananjaya rises up in an appeal along with his mates but gets no response from the umpire. They do not have the review left as well. It wouldn't have mattered as the replay shows that it was spinning down the leg side and would have missed the stumps.
On the hips, turned to the man at 45 for a single.
Akila Dananjaya is back on.
On middle and leg, helped towards mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and on middle, it's worked wide of mid on for a quick single. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end. Touch and go.
JP Duminy comes out to bat. He scored a brilliant unbeaten fifty in the previous game.

OUT! De Kock holes out! Misses out on a well-deserved hundred. Can Sri Lanka still believe? They have 83 runs to play with. For South Africa, plenty of balls left, 141 to be precise, so no need to panic yet. Rajitha has not come up with a wicket-taking ball. He is just lucky to get it. A delivery on de Kock's pads and nine out of 10 times he will put those away. But Rajitha has luck on his side this time. He mistimes his flick shot in the air and Suranga Lakmal moves across to his right from deep square leg to complete the catch. Quinton was dropped on 18 and 24 off Kasun's bowling and he finally manages to remove him from the crease for his first ODI wicket.
Coming in with the angle, tucked in front of square leg for a run.
Back of a length outside off, Faf shuffles a touch and plays it with an angled bat towards point.
Kasun Rajitha returns.
Uses his feet to this one and taps it with the spin through mid-wicket. A run taken.
Du Plessis turns this against the spin to short fine leg.
Shorter in length, de Kock cuts it towards third man for an easy run.
Allows the ball to come to him and then dabs it towards short third man.
Tossed up ball outside off, Quinton is nimble on his feet as he drives this one towards extra  cover.
Spinning down the leg side, turned to the man at 45.
Goes on the back foot and slaps it to deep cover for a run.
Fires this one in. Very full and outside off, du Plessis squeezes it out towards covers and crosses.

SIX! That has gone all the way. All timing, no power. Flighted full ball around leg, spinning back in a shade, du Plessis shimmies down the track and flicks it nonchalantly over mid-wicket. 90m in the radar.
Quicker one, on middle, it's blocked with a straight bat by Faf.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it with the spin to sweeper cover. A single to rotate the strike.
Short and wide outside off, de Kock plays a cracking square cut but it's stopped by the point fielder with a dive, a half stop that, but no run taken.
Du Plessis has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Knocks a full ball gently down to long on and brings up 150 for South Africa with a single.
Allows the ball to spin back in and then punches it to sweeper cover for a couple of runs. No pressure exerted from Sri Lanka.
Gets back and plays it down towards point.
Turning back into the batsman from outside off, shorter in length and staying low, de Kock moves back and hits it towards mid-wicket. Dot ball.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Tries to play the inside-out shot but mistimes it over backward point for a couple.
Tossed up ball, du Plessis kneels and fetches it from outside off to slog sweep it towards deep mid-wicket. A run this time.
Comes from 'round the wicket with a leg slip in place. Serves it full around leg and du Plessis flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Works it off his pads behind square leg and crosses.
De Kock has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gets on the front foot and drives it back.
Shehan Jayasuriya is into the attack for the first time.
FOUR! All class from Faf. Plays a perfect drop kick. Runs down to the pitch of the delivery and goes inside-out over extra cover. Good timing and placement. Another boundary for South Africa.
Faf has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

NOT OUT! No bat and it bounced as well. Hmm... Waste of technology, now Sri Lanka have none left. Tossed up ball around middle, turning in, de Kock fails to connect with his sweep shot and it goes off his pads, hits his elbow and then loops behind. Kusal Perera stretches across to his right and takes the ball before appealing. The bowler also joins but the umpire stays put. Angelo Mathews has a word with his keeper and then reluctantly goes for the DRS. The replays roll in and the Snicko finds no wood. Further, they show that it bounced before going into the gloves of Perera. To follow the whole procedure, the third umpire checks for the lbw as well. But the ball is turning too much and is missing the stumps. Nothing going Lanka's way.
Review time! It's for a catch taken behind by the keeper. But is there any bat involved? Let's wait and watch...
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Edged! Flighted and outside off, du Plessis edges his attempted drive past backward point and takes three runs.
Prabath Jayasuriya is back on.

FOUR! The extra ball costs Perera. He goes for another slower bouncer but this time de Kock is ready for it on his back foot. Rides the bounce and pulls it with all the control in the world for a boundary at deep square leg.

Slips a length ball down the leg side, de Kock tries to flick but misses. A nice try by the keeper and bowler as they appeal but umpire Paul Reiffel ain't getting fooled. He stretches his arms to signal a wide.
Another slower bouncer, around leg, de Kock pulls out at the last moment as he was shaping up for the horizontal bat shot.
Walks down the track and works it with the spin through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
On a length around middle and off, du Plessis defends it off his front foot.
Full and on middle, du Plessis forces it down to mid on where Tharanga makes a good diving stop. A rarity.
Loopy and full on off, Faf is forward in defense and it goes off the outer half of the bat to cover-point. They steal a single.
Full flighted around leg, de Kock sweeps it in front of square leg for one.
Once again hangs behind in the crease for a delivery spinning back in and then whips it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Allows the ball to spin back in and defends it from the crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted full ball on off, some puff of dust visible there as du Plessis leans forward to defend. Gets an inside edge and it goes off his pads to mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery on off, de Kock punches it off the back foot to deep point for a couple.
A slower bouncer, well-directed, de Kock gives a bit of a charge and then sways away at the last moment.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks.
Delivers it on the pads, Faf has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full in length and outside off, Faf drives it to the longer part of the ground and Lakmal at deep cover makes a diving stop. Saves two for his team.

FOUR! The southpaw is not allowing Akila to settle against him. Brings out the cross-batted shot this time, goes down on one knee and punishes the full length ball around leg with a paddle sweep. Fine connection and it speeds away to fine leg for a boundary. 9 from the over.
FOUR! De Kock holds the key, he is playing the spinners quite easily. Stretches out for a full ball around off and drills his drive through covers.
Quinton has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A full toss to greet the batsman. It's forced down to long on for a run.
Skipper Faf du Plessis in next.

OUT! Once again Aiden Markram has been hunted down by a spinner. For the umpteenth time on this tour. There is a serious issue with his technique. Once more he is found completely at sea while trying to pick up Dananjaya's variation. A well-disguised leg spinner, landing full outside off. Markram initially looks to give the charge but is beaten in flight. He then tries to stay back and defend it down but without knowing that the naughty ball will be spinning away from him. Ends up getting a faint edge behind and Kusal Perera makes no mistake. They appeal and the finger goes up. Markram in fact was already on his way. Everything was ugly about this wicket as far as the batsman is concerned. Markram's feet were all over the place. Could have played it with a big stride forward by staying inside the crease. He has to work really hard on his shortcomings.
A slip and leg slip in and Dananjaya bowls a full ball around middle. Aiden defends it back.

Drinks break. South Africa are cruising. 136 more needed. Sri Lanka have been lethargic in the field and have only themselves to blame. Quinton de Kock has got a start and he is going on nicely. The hosts need wickets and that too in a cluster to bounce back. Their spinners are capable of doing that but will their fielders support the cause?
FOUR! An overpitched ball outside off and de Kock drills it down the ground through mid off for a boundary.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Fullish and driven down towards mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Angling in, Aiden has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good length delivery outside off, left alone.
Thisara Perera is back on.
Walks down the track and pushes it towards point.
That hardly bounced, a grubber. De Kock reaches out for it and keeps it out off the bottom edge.
Driven towards the mid on region. One run added to the total.
Leans forward and pushes it back towards the right side of the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. They pick up a single.
Flatter and on off, worked through mid-wicket for one. 11 from the over.
Markram has played it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A conventional sweep by Quinton now. It travels to fine leg and the South African keeper travels to the other end.

FOUR! Courtesy another misfield, that has become a norm. Tharanga, the culprit. Another well-timed reverse sweep races away from de Kock's bat. Beats backward point and Tharanga in the deep makes a complete mess near the fence.

FOUR! 16th ODI fifty for Quinton de Kock. He has struck form after a hapless Test series. Brings out the reverse sweep again and nails his shot to perfection. Fetches a boundary behind backward point to achieve his milestone. Cannot afford to relax as he is the set batsman and needs to carry on. Finish the job, that should be his aim.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Aiden Markram walks out in the middle. Another spin test awaits him. So far, he has failed on this tour. Will the script change?

OUT! Stop the press, Sri Lanka have taken a catch. Only by just though as Dananjaya was in no control of it. A soft dismissal against the run of play, have to say. A friendly full toss by Akila, Amla advances down the track to meet the ball but ends up chipping it straight back. Dananjaya tries to catch it in his followthrough but it bursts out of his hands and he somehow manages to stick it back with his hands near his thigh. Phew. Are they allergic to the ball? Anyway, Hashim departs after giving a good start. 154 needed off 216 balls.
FOUR! Sweet timing! Loopy and full around off, Amla kneels down and sweeps it with excellent timing through backward square leg for a boundary. South Africa are cruising!
Flatter and shorter around off, too close for the square cut. Amla still attempts it but gets a bottom edge. Goes on one bounce to the keeper.

Another misfield. This is becoming comical. Floated full ball outside off, Amla goes down and across before sweeping it towards short fine leg. Tharanga dives there but fails to make a clean stop. They smuggle a couple of runs.
This time de Kock uses his feet to come down the track and hits it to long off for a run.
Comes down the track to a full ball and drives it through covers for a single.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Tickles it off his pads to fine leg and rotates the strike.
A flighted ball around leg, de Kock reverse sweeps it but finds the point fielder.
Attempts a reverse-batted shot to a straightforward delivery but fails to middle it. The bowler shouts for an lbw but nothing from the umpire. Maybe, it hit the arms of the batsman.
Gets forward to a full ball and threads his drive through covers for one.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. They pick up a single.
Good effort in the field for a change. A paddle sweep by Amla has been stopped by a diving effort from the short fine leg fielder. 7 from the over.
Flatter on off, Amla strokes it towards covers but not in the gap.
Amla dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Wide! Fires one down the leg side, Amla tries flicking but misses.
FOUR! It's spreading like an epidemic. Another misfield results in a boundary. A full toss on off, Amla thwacks it down the ground and Rajitha at mid off makes a complete mess.
Leans on the front foot and drives it through mid off for one.
Stays back and punches it through covers for a single.
Gets forward and drives it through covers for a single.
Arm ball going down leg, once again Amla fails to work it around.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Skidding down the leg side, Amla fails to middle his flick shot properly.
Gets on the front foot and drives it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Poor beginning. Bowls it down the leg side and Amla easily paddles it down to fine leg for a boundary. Once again the over starts on a sorry note for Sri Lanka.

End of Powerplay 1. Now, a maximum of 4 fielders are allowed outside the ring until the 40th over as debutant Prabath Jayasuriya comes into the attack. Meanwhile, Kusal Perera has donned the gloves as Niroshan Dickwella leaves the field. He hurt his ribs while batting and it seems that he has aggravated that injury while collecting the ball behind the stumps on ball number 4.3.
De Kock has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. 11 from the over, 178 needed off 240 balls.

FOUR! South Africa are dominating proceedings here and Sri Lanka have a big part to play in it. Short in length and wide outside off, de Kock camps back and whacks it square of the wicket on the off side. Lakmal stationed there at cover-point lets it through his legs. Mathews is very disappointed.
On the pads again, Amla helps it in front of square leg for another single in this over.
Leans forward and drives it through mid off for a run.
Flatter and on middle, eased towards square leg for a single.

FOUR! Excellent start to the over for South Africa. Dananjaya flights this one up and bowls it full and down the leg side. Amla sits down on one knee and sweeps it past the short fine leg fielder for a boundary.
Shortish and outside off, played down to point.

FOUR! Finds the gap! Once again Perera is very full with his length outside off. De Kock hits it hard and tries to go over covers. The ball bounces once inside the ring, beats the diving fielder and then races away to the boundary line.
Serves it full and outside off, it's hit down the ground towards mid off.
Very full and outside off, de Kock squeezes it out through the line but finds the cover-point fielder.
Fullish and on middle, clipped through square leg for one.
Beaten! A little bit of movement off the deck as it lands on a length outside off. Amla pushes inside the line and misses.
Thisara Perera is into the attack.
SIX! High and handsome! 50 up for South Africa. A flighted ball around middle and leg, de Kock shimmies down the track and towers it over long on for a maximum.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched off the back foot but straight towards the cover fielder.
Tossed up ball on off, de Kock is forward in defense and it goes off the shoulder of the bat to point.
Quinton has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted and full on off, from 'round the wicket, de Kock defends it off his front foot.
Advances down the track and pushes it towards mid off for a brisk single. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end otherwise it would have been interesting.
Akila Dananjaya comes into the attack. The real test begins now for South Africa. They have a platform now and can manipulate the tweakers. Let's see how they approach.
Good length ball on off, it's defended off the back foot to end the over.
On the pads, helped towards square leg.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Stays on the back foot and taps a length ball towards the point fielder.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Short in length around off, Amla rises on his back foot and with his one leg in the air, he pulls it behind square leg. Timing is exquisite and it races through.
Play and a miss! Back of a length delivery wide outside off, Amla tries to punch it through the line but misses.
A mini-conference going on. Angelo Mathews calls his players and is having a word. Rightly so, they have been dismal so far in the field.
Around middle and leg, flicked off the pads to square leg. Dot ball to end another eventful over, 10 runs from it along with two dropped catches.

Misfield this time. Results in a FOUR! What are Sri Lanka up to? Debutant Prabath Jayasuriya has let it through his legs. Under immense pressure, the Lankans on the field. A low full toss outside off, Quinton pushes it through the line, straight towards the extra cover fielder who lets it through.

DROPPED AGAIN! This time Rajitha has put down a return catch. Full and on middle, de Kock chips it straight back and Rajitha sticks out his right hand. Fails to pouch it and another chance goes down begging.
Turns it off his pads on the leg side, finds the gap and picks up a couple of runs.
FOUR! Adding salt to the wound. Rajitha delivers it wide outside off, de Kock reaches out for it and blazes it through the extra cover region for a delightful boundary.

Another dropped catch! Akila Dananjaya is the culprit this time. Look at Rajitha's face. The debutant cannot believe his luck, two drops off his bowling already, both the openers have got a life each now. This is extremely poor from Sri Lanka. A full length ball around leg has been flicked uppishly off his pads by Quinton. It goes in and out of Akila's hands standing in front of square leg. Feeling really bad for Kasun. Poor lad cannot vent out much frustration either. Sri Lanka need to pull up their socks in the field.
On a length and wide outside off, Amla reaches out for it and strokes it through the line. Finds the extra cover fielder.
FOUR! This is trademark Amla. Shuffles across his stumps to a length ball outside off and clips it through backward square leg for a boundary.
Lakmal trying out everything. This one is an outswinger outside off. Leaving the batsman. Amla once again is very watchful as he allows it through.
Good leave. It's on a length outside off, shaping back in off the seam, Amla covers the line and shoulders arms. Dickwella tumbles across to his left to collect the ball.
Sliding down the leg side, Amla nudges it fine down the leg side and returns for the second run.
Uses his hand-eye coordination to punch it through the line but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

FOUR! Fine shot! A little bit too full this time, around middle and leg, de Kock meets it with a straight blade and drives it back past the bowler. It races through and reaches the fence in no time. Eventful over, 7 coming from it.

DROPPED BY KUSAL PERERA! Oh dear, that's a dreadful miss. A length ball angling into the batsman, Amla flicks it across the line albeit uppishly and it goes straight towards the fielder at mid-wicket. Perera reacts quickly to get his hands on it but fails to hold on to the catch. Can prove to be costly, they are not defending a big total. They pick up a single.
Hangs on the back foot to a shortish ball outside off and punches it towards the cover fielder.
Lands it on a length and close to the off stump line, Amla sticks back to defend it back.
Goes full on this occasion, around off, Amla drives it down the ground but finds mid on.
Good length ball around off, angling in, Amla stays back to punch it past the left side of the mid-wicket fielder. A couple of runs taken.
De Kock steps down the track and Lakmal continues to bowl the same length. The batsmen punches it square of the wicket on the off side.
Back of a length ball, Quinton once again gives himself some room and chops it to point.
De Kock makes some room, eyeing his favourite area. Cuts the shortish ball past point. Rajitha in the deep moves to his left and slides to stop a couple for his side.
Short of a length ball outside off, de Kock punches it off the back foot to the cover region.
A length ball angling across Quinton as he taps it with soft hands to covers.
Shortish ball around off, de Kock answers it with a straight bat.
Short of a length around off, pushed off the back foot to the cover region.
If he missed that, he would have been a candidate for LBW. Fuller length ball, angling in. Amla's bat comes down at an angle as he gets an inside edge onto his pads.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Amla is off the mark too! Works a length ball off his pads through square leg and picks up a couple.
Streaky! Good length ball on middle, de Kock tries to get behind it but gets an outside edge down to third man. A run taken.
A full ball well outside off, de Kock goes after it but gets beaten.
The debutant, Kasun Rajitha to bowl with the second new ball from the other end.
Fullish ball on middle, driven past the diving mid on fielder. Three runs is the result. 11 from the first over.
Ouch! That will sting. Good length ball, takes off after pitching. De Kock tries to play it to the off side but the extra bounce deceives him. He gets hit on the gloves.

FOUR! After such a good effort from Mathews, Jayasuriya has made a meal of one. Short and some room on offer, de Kock cuts it towards Shehan who is sloppy in the point region and the ball goes past him to the fence.
FOUR! South Africa and de Kock are away! A length ball around off, de Kock leans ahead and strokes it crisply through covers to find the fence.

Brilliant fielding from Mathews! Sri Lanka will need much more of that throughout the game. Fuller length ball outside off, de Kock drives it crisply towards covers where Angelo dives full length to his right to save certain runs for his side.
Starts off with a length ball on leg stump, de Kock tucks it with a closed bat face towards mid-wicket.

We are back for the chase. The players and the umpires make their way out to the middle again. Quinton de Kock and Hashim Amla to open the batting for South Africa. Suranga Lakmal to bowl with the first new ball. A slip in place. Here we go...
